source_text: VI. Καὶ ἐπιμενόντων τῶν ζητούντων αὐτόν, μετέβη εἰς ἕτερον ἀγρίδιον. Καὶ εὐθέως ἐπέστησαν οἱ ζητοῦντες αὐτόν. Καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες συνελάβοντο παιδάρια δύο, ὧν τὸ ἕτερον βασανιζόμενον ὡμολόγησεν. Ἦν γὰρ καὶ ἀδύνατον λαθεῖν αὐτόν, ἐπεὶ καὶ οἱ προδιδόντες αὐτὸν οἰκεῖοι ὑπῆρχον. Καὶ ὁ εἰρήναρχος, ὁ κεκληρωμένος τὸ αὐτὸ ὄνομα, Ἡρώδης ἐπιλεγόμενος, ἔσπευσεν εἰς τὸ στάδιον αὐτὸν εἰσαγαγεῖν, ἵνα ἐκεῖνος μὲν τὸν ἴδιον κλῆρον ἀπαρτίσῃ, Χριστοῦ κοινωνὸς γενόμενος, οἱ δὲ προδόντες αὐτὸν τῆς αὐτῆς τοῦ Ἰούδα τύχωσιν τιμωρίας.
thought_title: Betrayal by members of his own household
orientation: Polycarp has withdrawn to a country place outside the city to pray while men are searching for him to arrest him.
pass_a_gloss: And while those seeking him persisted, he moved to another small farm. And immediately those seeking him came upon it. And not having found him, they seized two little boys, of whom the one, while being tortured, confessed. For it was even impossible for him to escape notice, since even those handing him over were of his household. And the police chief, the one assigned the same name, the one called Herod, hurried to bring him into the stadium, in order that that man on the one hand might complete his own appointed lot, having become a sharer of Christ, and those having betrayed him on the other hand might obtain the same punishment as Judas.

choices.why: literal diminutive plural, keeps age and low status without deciding legal status
fixed glossary English for this verb, even though here it discloses a hiding place under torture
fixed glossary English for the local arresting officer

choices.english: might complete his own appointed lot
choices.why: literal lot language with purpose force, not a general destiny idea

pass_b_english: As the men searching for him kept at it, he moved to another small country place. They arrived there at once, and when they did not find him, they seized two little boys. One of them confessed while under torture. He could not possibly escape notice, for even those who betrayed him belonged to his own household (Matthew 10:36).

The police chief who bore the same name, called Herod, then hurried to bring him into the stadium, so that he might complete his own appointed lot by sharing in Christ, and those who betrayed him might suffer the same punishment as Judas.
